title: Place Exposed to the Sun
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, and the local precinct's role generally filled by Megure) are handled per convention except that the one-off local officer Daimatsu is kept as a minor node since he is uniquely named for this episode and has plot-relevant dialogue (receives the alibi checks and the final accusation). No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. Per the 2026-08 batch-8 scoping change, temporal fields (order/temporal_frame/years_before_present) are omitted entirely. Old cases/ep315 file's culprit (Kuroki) and core motive (uncredited ghost-painting, denied contest entry) check out against the transcript -- no reversal here, unlike some other rebuilds. What the old file missed/flattened: it collapsed everything into 3 generic `events` and a single location; the transcript actually supports 6 distinct locations, a forged suicide note, a pre-recorded-voice alibi trick, two separate paintings (the Mt Fuji piece Kuroki secretly finished for Seizan, and the portrait of Ran Kuroki painted for the contest under his own name), and a genuinely comparative clue about the white powder on Kuroki's feet (initially explained away as his oyster-shell whitewash paint pigment, actually bamboo sawdust matching the cut stalks at the scene) plus a second comparative clue tying the bamboo-growth journal's rates to the official time-of-death window to explain how the murder was physically possible during Kuroki's fishing alibi. The old file also omitted Yamamoto Noriko's resolution: she was suspected purely on opportunity/timing (seen pale near the forest right when the nightingales' alarm cry sounded) with no motive ever stated in dialogue, and her alibi (at the hospital with her sick mother during the 11:00-13:00 TOD window) held -- no `has_motive_against` edge invented for her since none is supported by the transcript. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: White powder on Kuroki's feet: he claims it's oyster-shell whitewash paint pigment (matching the powder paints in his workroom), but it's actually bamboo sawdust matching the stalks cut down at the clearing -- proves he was at the murder scene cutting bamboo, not just mixing paint.

Seizan's own bamboo-growth journal (30cm, then 60cm, then 2m after rain) shows a shoot can grow far enough within a couple of hours to strangle someone -- explains how the murder happened inside the 11:00-13:00 estimated time of death while Kuroki was fishing with an alibi.
